messages.content: Why did Drona ask Ekalavya for his thumb?
Ekalavya had learned archery alone in front of a clay image of Drona and had become better than Arjuna. Drona asked for his right thumb as a teacher's fee, and Ekalavya gave it gladly.
Why is a raga more than just a scale?
A scale only lists the notes. A raga also decides which notes are strong or weak, how phrases move, and which mood and time suit it.
Why did King Dasaratha have to send Rama away to the forest?
Long ago he had promised Queen Kaikeyi two boons. She used them to ask that her son Bharat be made heir and that Rama be exiled for fourteen years.
What does the wedge-pulling monkey teach in the Panchatantra?
Do not meddle in work you do not understand. A monkey pulls the wedge out of a half-split log and is caught when the two halves snap shut.
What does young Pip take from home for the convict on the marshes?
He takes bread, cheese, mincemeat, brandy and a pork pie from the pantry, and a file from Joe's forge so the man can get his leg iron off.
Why is young Jane locked in the red-room at Gateshead?
Her cousin John Reed throws a book at her, and she fights back. Mrs. Reed punishes her by shutting her in the red-room, where Mr. Reed had died.
Why does Jonathan Harker travel to Transylvania?
He is a young solicitor sent to help Count Dracula buy a house in England. The property is an old estate near London called Carfax.
What is the famous first line of Pride and Prejudice?
"It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife."
Who tells the story in Wuthering Heights?
Mr. Lockwood, the new tenant of Thrushcross Grange, begins it. Most of the story is then told to him by the housekeeper, Nelly Dean.
Why is Irene Adler always "the woman" to Sherlock Holmes?
In A Scandal in Bohemia she sees through his disguise and slips away with the photograph he was hired to recover. Holmes respects her cleverness ever after.
Whom does Natasha Rostova marry by the end of War and Peace?
She marries Pierre Bezukhov. In the epilogue, several years later, they have three daughters and a son, and Natasha is a devoted wife and mother.
How does the narrator of Moby-Dick introduce himself in the first line?
He says, "Call me Ishmael." He explains that he goes to sea whenever he feels gloomy and restless on land.
How is the story of Frankenstein framed?
It begins with letters from the explorer Robert Walton to his sister, Mrs. Saville. Walton rescues Victor on the Arctic ice and writes down his tale.
What happens when Alice drinks from the bottle labelled "DRINK ME"?
She shrinks until she is only ten inches high. Then she realizes she has left the little golden key on the table, far out of reach.
How did the Pandavas escape from the house of lac?
Vidura warned them and sent a miner who dug a hidden passage. The Pandavas set the house on fire themselves and slipped out through the tunnel, while Purochana died in the flames.
In a raga, what do vadi and samvadi mean?
The vadi is the most important note, and the samvadi is the second most important. They act as resting points and emotional centres, not just loud notes.
Who turned Kaikeyi against Rama?
Manthara, her hunchbacked maid. She warned Kaikeyi that if Rama became king, she and Bharat would lose their honour and power.
Why does the hungry jackal stop fearing the loud sound in the forest?
He finds it is only a war-drum that booms when grasses sway against it. He even creeps inside hoping for fat, but finds only wood and skin.
What did Arjuna do at Draupadi's swayamvara?
Dressed as a Brahmana, he strung the very stiff bow that the kings had failed to bend and shot down the mark set up above a machine in the sky. That won him Draupadi.
Who turns out to be Pip's secret benefactor in Great Expectations?
It is Abel Magwitch, the convict Pip helped as a boy. Pip had believed all along that the money came from Miss Havisham.
Who is Helen Burns in Jane Eyre?
Helen is Jane's first real friend at school. She is patient and forgiving, and she dies of consumption with Jane lying beside her.
What does Harker notice while shaving with the Count behind him?
The Count does not appear in the shaving glass. Harker cuts himself in surprise, and the Count makes a grab at his throat when he sees the blood.
What does Darcy say about Elizabeth at the Meryton assembly?
He says she is tolerable but not handsome enough to tempt him. Elizabeth overhears and later tells the story to her friends with great humour.
Where does Mr. Earnshaw find Heathcliff?
On a trip to Liverpool he finds him starving and homeless in the streets. He carries him home to Wuthering Heights wrapped in his greatcoat.
What is the real purpose of the Red-Headed League?
It keeps the pawnbroker Jabez Wilson away from his shop, copying the Encyclopaedia every day. Meanwhile his assistant digs a tunnel from the cellar to a bank.
In War and Peace, who becomes Nikolai Rostov's wife?
Nikolai marries Princess Mary Bolkonskaya, Prince Andrew's sister. They settle at Bald Hills, where he becomes a hard-working, careful landowner.
How do Ishmael and Queequeg first meet?
The Spouter-Inn is full, so the landlord makes Ishmael share a bed with Queequeg, a tattooed harpooneer from a South Sea island. Ishmael is scared at first, but they soon become close friends.
Where does Victor Frankenstein go to university?
He studies at Ingolstadt. There he becomes obsessed with discovering the secret of life.
Where does the pool of tears in Alice in Wonderland come from?
When Alice grows to nine feet tall, she cries buckets. Later she shrinks again and nearly drowns in the pool of her own tears.
What is a pakad?
A pakad is the identifying phrase of a raga. A listener may recognize the raga from its pakad even before hearing the full scale.
What did Yudhishthira lose in the game of dice?
Playing against Sakuni, who threw the dice for Duryodhana, he lost his wealth, his kingdom, his brothers, himself and finally Draupadi.
Why did the sage Visvamitra take young Rama away from Ayodhya?
He needed Rama's help against demons who were spoiling his sacrifices. On the way, Rama killed the fierce demoness Tadaka.
How do the crows get rid of the black snake that eats their chicks?
The crow-hen steals a golden chain from some royal women bathing in a pond and drops it into the snake's hole. The king's men follow, find the snake, and kill it with clubs.
What happened at the lake guarded by the Yaksha?
Four Pandava brothers drank without answering the Yaksha's questions and fell dead. Yudhishthira answered every question, and the Yaksha, who was really Dharma, brought them back to life.
Why have all the clocks at Satis House stopped?
Miss Havisham stopped them at twenty minutes to nine, the moment she learned her bridegroom had abandoned her. She still wears her yellowed wedding dress.
Who is Jane's pupil at Thornfield?
Her pupil is Adele Varens, a lively little French girl who is Mr. Rochester's ward.
What strange thing does Harker see the Count do on the castle wall?
He sees the Count crawl head first down the wall, face down, with his cloak spreading around him like great wings.
Whom does Mr. Collins marry after Elizabeth refuses him?
He marries Charlotte Lucas, Elizabeth's friend, within days of the refusal. Charlotte accepts because she wants a comfortable home.
Why does Heathcliff suddenly leave Wuthering Heights as a young man?
He overhears Catherine telling Nelly it would degrade her to marry him. He leaves before he hears her say how much she loves him.
What killed Julia Stoner in The Speckled Band?
A swamp adder, a deadly snake sent by her stepfather, Dr. Grimesby Roylott. It came through a ventilator and down a dummy bell-rope.
What does the word thaat mean in Hindustani music?
A thaat is a parent scale used to classify ragas. It helps organize them but does not fully define them; two ragas from the same thaat can sound very different.
How does Pierre Bezukhov suddenly become one of the richest men in Russia?
Pierre is the illegitimate son of old Count Bezukhov. When the count dies, Pierre is made his legal heir and inherits the whole fortune.
In Moby-Dick, how did Captain Ahab lose his leg?
The white whale bit it off on an earlier voyage. Ahab now stands on an ivory leg made from the polished bone of a sperm whale's jaw.
Who is wrongly executed for the murder of little William?
Justine Moritz, a young woman who lives with the Frankenstein family. The creature placed the picture William had been carrying in her pocket.
Who wins the Caucus-race?
The Dodo declares that everybody has won and all must have prizes. Alice hands out comfits from her pocket.
What was the golden deer that Sita wanted?
It was the demon Maricha in disguise, sent by Ravan. While Rama chased it, Ravan carried Sita away.
What trick does the old heron play on the fish in his pond?
He says fishermen are coming and offers to carry the fish to a safer pond. Instead he eats them on a rock, until a crab sees the bones and cuts off his head.
Who blocked Bhima's path with his tail in the forest?
An old monkey lay across the path, and Bhima could not even lift its tail. The monkey was Hanuman, who was also a son of the wind-god and so Bhima's brother.
Which notes are missing in Raga Bhoopali?
Bhoopali has no Ma and no Ni, so it uses only five notes. It is a peaceful evening raga from the Kalyan family.
What is Joe Gargery's job?
Joe is the village blacksmith. He is married to Pip's sister and is a kind, gentle friend to Pip.
How does Jane meet Mr. Rochester for the first time?
On an icy lane his horse slips and falls, and Rochester sprains his ankle. Jane helps him back onto his horse without knowing who he is.
How does Count Dracula reach England?
He sails on the ship Demeter, which is driven ashore at Whitby in a storm. The crew have vanished, and the dead captain is tied to the wheel.
Why will the Longbourn estate go to Mr. Collins?
The estate is entailed on the male line, and Mr. Bennet has no son. So it will pass to his cousin, Mr. Collins.
Whom does Catherine Earnshaw marry?
She marries Edgar Linton of Thrushcross Grange. She tells Nelly she will accept him partly because he is handsome, rich and fond of her.
Where is the blue carbuncle found?
It is found in the crop of a Christmas goose. The commissionaire's wife discovers it while preparing the bird.
Why was Devavrata given the name Bhishma?
To let his father marry Satyavati, he vowed never to claim the throne and never to marry. Because the vow was so terrible, he was called Bhishma.
What did Jatayus do when Ravan carried off Sita?
The old king of the vultures attacked Ravan and broke his chariot, but Ravan cut off his wings. Jatayus lived just long enough to tell Rama what had happened.
What happens to the Brahman who daydreams over his jar of barley-meal?
He imagines selling the meal, buying goats, cows and horses, and starting a family. Lost in his dream, he kicks out, smashes the jar, and is covered in white meal.
Lying wounded at Austerlitz, what does Prince Andrew notice above him?
He sees the lofty, endless sky with grey clouds moving across it. Next to it, the battle and even his hero Napoleon suddenly seem small and unimportant.
What reward does Ahab promise to whoever first sights the white whale?
He nails a gold Spanish doubloon to the mainmast. The first man to raise Moby Dick will win it.
How does Frankenstein's creature learn to speak?
He hides in a hovel next to the De Lacey family's cottage and watches them through a small crack. He learns words by listening, especially when Felix teaches Safie.
What does the Caterpillar ask Alice when they meet?
He asks, "Who are you?" She finds it hard to answer because she has changed size so many times that day.
My teacher says Raga Bhairav sounds serious. Which notes give it that colour?
Komal Re and komal Dha, sung slowly and with weight. Bhairav is a prayerful morning raga.
How did Damayanti find the real Nala among the gods at her swayamvara?
Four gods came looking exactly like Nala. Damayanti prayed to them and then saw that the gods did not sweat or blink and did not touch the ground, while Nala did. So she chose him.
Who was Surpanakha, and why was she punished?
She was Ravan's sister. She wanted Rama as her husband and rushed at Sita in jealousy, so Lakshman cut off her nose and ears.
In The Mice That Ate Iron, how does Naduk get his balance-beam back?
He hides the cheating merchant's son and claims a hawk carried the boy off. When the merchant says that is impossible, Naduk answers that so is mice eating iron.
Who are Estella's real parents?
Her father is Magwitch, and her mother is Molly, Mr. Jaggers's housekeeper. Miss Havisham adopted her as a small child.
Why can Jane's wedding to Rochester not go ahead?
A lawyer and Richard Mason announce that Rochester already has a wife. She is Bertha Mason, who is kept locked on the third storey of Thornfield.
Which three men propose to Lucy Westenra on the same day?
Dr. Seward, Quincey Morris and Arthur Holmwood all propose to her. She accepts Arthur.
How does Jane Bennet end up staying at Netherfield?
Her mother sends her on horseback when rain is likely, so she will have to stay the night. Jane is caught in the rain, falls ill, and stays for several days.
How does Catherine first come to stay at Thrushcross Grange?
She and Heathcliff go to spy on the Lintons, and the bulldog Skulker seizes her ankle. She stays there for five weeks while it heals.
Who is the beggar Hugh Boone?
He is Neville St. Clair in disguise. St. Clair earned far more by begging in the City than by honest work and kept it secret from his family.
Who killed Kichaka at King Virata's court?
Bhima did. Kichaka kept harassing Draupadi, so Bhima told her to arrange a night meeting with Kichaka in the empty dancing hall, and Bhima waited there in her place.
How is Malkauns different from Chandrakauns?
Both are pentatonic late-night ragas. Malkauns uses komal Ni, while Chandrakauns uses shuddha Ni, which gives it a brighter, dreamy shade.
Why does Pierre fight a duel with Dolokhov?
Pierre suspects Dolokhov of an affair with his wife Helene, and Dolokhov provokes him at a dinner. Pierre has hardly held a pistol before, yet he wounds Dolokhov.
How does Ishmael survive the final wreck?
He floats on Queequeg's coffin, which had been turned into a life-buoy. After almost a day and a night, the ship Rachel picks him up.
Which books does the creature find and read?
He finds Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch's Lives and The Sorrows of Werter. They teach him about history and feelings and deepen his loneliness.
What is strange about the way the Cheshire Cat disappears?
It vanishes slowly, starting with the end of its tail and ending with its grin, which stays in the air for some time after the rest has gone.
When Arjuna and Duryodhana both asked Krishna for help, what did each choose?
Arjuna chose Krishna himself, even though he would not fight. Duryodhana gladly took Krishna's large army of Narayana soldiers.
How did Sugriva become king of the Vanars?
Rama killed Bali, Sugriva's brother, with an arrow during their fight. Sugriva then became king and sent his Vanars to search for Sita.
Why do the mice rescue the trapped elephant-king?
Earlier he had agreed to take another path so his herd would stop crushing them. When he was caught in a trap, the mice gnawed through the ropes and set the herd free.
What do audav, shadav and sampurna mean?
They tell how many notes a raga uses. Audav means five notes, shadav means six, and sampurna means all seven.
Who is the 'pale young gentleman' that Pip fights at Satis House?
He is Herbert Pocket. Years later they meet again in London, share rooms, and become close friends; Herbert even nicknames Pip Handel.
What does St. John Rivers ask Jane to do?
He asks her to marry him and go with him to India as a missionary's wife. Jane refuses to marry him because he does not love her.
In Dracula, who is Van Helsing?
He is a doctor and professor from Amsterdam and Dr. Seward's old teacher. He works out what is attacking Lucy and leads the hunt for the Count.
Who runs away with Lydia Bennet?
Lydia elopes with Mr. Wickham from Brighton. Darcy secretly pays Wickham's debts and arranges for the two to marry.
Whom does Heathcliff marry, and why?
He marries Isabella Linton, Edgar's sister, mostly to hurt the Lintons. He treats her cruelly, and she later runs away to the south.
What arrives in the post in The Five Orange Pips?
An envelope containing five dried orange pips, with the letters K. K. K. written inside. Each man who receives one soon meets his death.
How could Sanjaya describe the war to the blind king Dhritarashtra?
The sage Vyasa gave Sanjaya divine sight. He could see everything happening on the battlefield and report it to the king.
Which man tries to run away with Natasha while Prince Andrew is abroad?
Anatole Kuragin, Helene's brother. The elopement is stopped, and Natasha learns that Anatole is already married.
Who is Starbuck on Ahab's ship?
Starbuck is the chief mate, a careful Quaker from Nantucket. He thinks it is madness to take revenge on a dumb animal and tries to turn Ahab from his hunt.
What does the creature ask Victor to make for him?
He asks for a female companion like himself. He promises that the two of them will go to the wilds of South America and never be seen by people again.
Why is it always tea-time at the Mad Tea-Party?
The Hatter says Time has been angry with him since the Queen's concert. So it is always six o'clock, and they never have time to wash the things.
What happened when the giants set Hanuman's tail on fire?
They wound strips of cotton cloth soaked in oil round his tail and set it alight. Hanuman broke free and used the burning tail to set the city of Lanka ablaze.
What happens to the bird who tells a monkey that the firefly is not fire?
The cold monkey ignores her and keeps blowing on it. When she keeps shouting in his ear, he grabs her and dashes her against a rock.
What is the difference between an alap and a taan?
An alap is the slow exploration of a raga without percussion. A taan is a fast melodic run, and it must still follow the raga's rules.
Why did Bhishma refuse to fight Sikhandin?
Sikhandin had been born a woman, so Bhishma would not strike him. Arjuna shot from behind Sikhandin, and Bhishma fell onto a bed of arrows.
What is unusual about Wemmick's house in Walworth?
Wemmick calls it the Castle. It has a tiny drawbridge, a flagstaff and a little gun fired every night, and he lives there with his deaf old father, the Aged.
How does Jane Eyre become rich?
Her uncle John Eyre of Madeira leaves her twenty thousand pounds. She shares it equally with her newly found cousins, Diana, Mary and St. John.
Why does Lucy's mother take away the garlic flowers?
She thinks they make the room stuffy, so she removes them and opens the window to let in fresh air. This lets the Count reach Lucy again.
Why does Lady Catherine de Bourgh come to Longbourn?
She has heard a report that Elizabeth will marry Darcy. She demands a promise that Elizabeth will never accept him, and Elizabeth refuses to give it.
What does Lockwood dream when he spends the night at the Heights?
He dreams that an icy child's hand grips his through the window. A voice sobs, "Let me in," and says it is Catherine Linton.
How does the engineer Victor Hatherley lose his thumb?
He is trapped in a hydraulic press by a gang of coiners. While escaping from a window, he is struck with a heavy cleaver and loses his thumb.
How did Abhimanyu die in the great war?
He broke into Drona's circular battle array, but the others could not follow him in. Surrounded by many warriors at once, he was finally killed.
What is a bandish?
A bandish is a fixed composition. It gives the raga a melodic and rhythmic home and shows a learner how the raga breathes.
Who built the bridge across the sea to Lanka?
Nala, a Vanar who was the son of Visvakarma, the builder of the gods. The army helped by carrying trees and rocks to the shore.
What becomes of the three fishes Forethought, Readywit and Fatalist?
Forethought leaves the lake before the fishermen arrive. Readywit plays dead in the net and slips back into the water, but Fatalist struggles in the net and is killed.
Who is Platon Karataev, and why does he matter to Pierre?
He is a simple peasant soldier whom Pierre meets as a prisoner of the French. His calm kindness and acceptance of life change the way Pierre sees the world.
What story does Father Mapple preach about in the whalemen's chapel?
He preaches about Jonah, who tried to run away from God and was swallowed by a great fish. He climbs into the high pulpit by a ship's side ladder and then pulls it up after him.
Why does Victor destroy the second creature he is building?
Working on a remote island in the Orkneys, he fears the two creatures might have children and become a danger to all people. He tears the half-made body to pieces.
What do the players use as balls and mallets in the Queen's croquet game?
The balls are live hedgehogs and the mallets are live flamingoes. The soldiers bend over to make the arches.
How was Drona made to give up fighting?
Bhima killed an elephant named Aswatthaman and shouted that Aswatthaman was dead. Drona believed his son had died, especially when Yudhishthira confirmed it, and lost the will to fight.
Who attacks Mrs. Joe in Great Expectations?
Orlick, Joe's surly journeyman, strikes her on the head. Years later, when he traps Pip in a lonely hut on the marshes near a limekiln, he boasts that he did it.
What happens to Thornfield Hall while Jane is away?
Bertha sets it on fire and dies after jumping from the roof. Rochester loses one hand and his eyesight while trying to save people.
What does Renfield eat in the asylum?
He catches flies, feeds them to spiders, and feeds the spiders to sparrows. He then eats the creatures himself, believing he can take in their lives.
What does Darcy's letter reveal to Elizabeth?
It explains why he separated Bingley from Jane, and it reveals that Wickham once tried to elope with Darcy's young sister, Georgiana. Elizabeth realizes she has misjudged both men.
How does young Cathy help Hareton Earnshaw?
She teaches him to read. Their lessons turn an unhappy quarrel into friendship, and by the end they plan to marry.
What odd requests does Violet Hunter face at the Copper Beeches?
She must cut her long hair short, wear an electric-blue dress and sit where she is told. Her employers are making her look like their daughter, who is kept locked up.
Name the ten commonly taught thaats.
They are Bilawal, Kalyan, Khamaj, Kafi, Bhairav, Bhairavi, Asavari, Todi, Marwa and Poorvi.
Why did Vibhishan leave Lanka and join Rama?
He advised his brother Ravan to give Sita back, but Ravan answered him with insults. Vibhishan then went over to Rama, who welcomed him.
How do three rogues trick the Brahman out of his goat?
One after another, they meet him and call the goat a dog, a dead calf and a donkey. He decides it must be a goblin, throws it down and runs home.
What vow did Arjuna make after his son Abhimanyu was killed?
He vowed to kill Jayadratha before sunset the next day or enter a fire himself. He kept the vow just before the sun went down.
What happens to Petya, the youngest Rostov son?
Petya joins Denisov's band of partisans and is killed in a raid on a French convoy. His death breaks his mother's heart.
What happens to little Pip, the youngest boy on Ahab's ship?
Pip panics, jumps from a whale-boat, and is left alone in the open sea for a while. He is rescued, but from then on he goes about the deck like an idiot, as the sailors say.
What happens to Henry Clerval?
Clerval is strangled by the creature. Victor is arrested in Ireland for the murder and lies ill for two months before he is cleared.
Why are the three gardeners painting the roses red?
They planted a white rose-tree by mistake instead of a red one. They hope to cover it up before the Queen finds out and has their heads cut off.
What are mandra, madhya and taar saptak?
They are the three octaves. Mandra is the lower octave, madhya is the middle octave, and taar is the upper octave.
How did Karna die?
His chariot wheel sank into the earth. While he was down from his chariot trying to lift it free, Arjuna shot him dead.
Whom does Joe marry after his first wife dies?
Joe marries Biddy, the kind young woman who once helped Pip with his lessons. They later name their little son Pip.
Who is Grace Poole at Thornfield?
Grace Poole is a servant. Jane is told that the strange laughter comes from her, but she is really the keeper of Rochester's wife, Bertha.
How does Mina help the vampire hunters?
She types out all the diaries, letters and newspaper cuttings and puts them in order. Reading them together, the men can follow the Count's movements.
With whom does Elizabeth visit Pemberley?
She goes with her aunt and uncle, Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner, on a tour of Derbyshire. Darcy surprises them by arriving home a day early.
Who is Linton Heathcliff?
He is the weak, sickly son of Heathcliff and Isabella. Heathcliff forces him to marry young Cathy so that he can gain Thrushcross Grange.
Who is Hosmer Angel in A Case of Identity?
He is Miss Sutherland's stepfather, Mr. Windibank, in disguise. He courted her himself so that she would not marry and he could keep using her income.
Who was Kumbhakarna?
He was Ravan's giant brother. Brahma had doomed him to sleep for six months at a time and wake for only a day; Ravan had him roused to fight, and Rama killed him.
How does Haughty, the huge black snake, meet his end?
He hurts himself squeezing through a narrow crack in his ant-hill. The ants, drawn by the smell of blood, swarm over him and sting him to death.
Who drove Karna's chariot in his last battle?
Salya, king of the Madras. He kept discouraging Karna by praising Arjuna.
Which ragas does the practice plan suggest for the monsoon?
It lists Miyan ki Malhar, Megh and Desh. Megh is a pentatonic rain raga with no Ga or Dha.
What kind of teacher is old Prince Bolkonski to his daughter Mary?
He is strict and impatient. He gives her geometry and algebra lessons himself and loses his temper when she does not understand.
Can you tell me who Stubb and Flask are?
Stubb is the second mate, easy-going and almost never without his pipe. Flask is the third mate, a short, stout young man from Martha's Vineyard.
What is the creature's threat about Victor's wedding night?
He says, "I shall be with you on your wedding-night." Victor thinks he himself is in danger, but the creature kills his bride, Elizabeth.
What happens to the Duchess's baby after Alice carries it outside?
It turns into a pig. Alice sets it down, and it trots quietly away into the wood.
How did Hanuman bring help when the princes lay wounded on the battlefield?
He flew to a mountain of healing herbs. When he could not pick out the right plants, he tore off the whole peak and carried it back.
How does the quarrel between the partridge and the rabbit end?
They ask a holy-seeming tomcat named Curd-Ear to judge it. He coaxes them close, then seizes and eats them both.
Where did Duryodhana hide at the end of the war?
He hid inside a lake, making the water stand still around him. The Pandavas found him, and Bhima beat him in a mace fight by breaking his thighs.
How does Miss Havisham get badly burned?
Her dress catches fire from the fireplace. Pip throws his two coats and the great cloth from the table over her to smother the flames, and burns both his own hands.
What does Jane do when she finds Rochester's bed on fire?
She throws water from the basin and jug over the flames and wakes him. Rochester asks her to tell no one about it.
How is Count Dracula finally destroyed?
Jonathan cuts his throat with his great Kukri knife, and Quincey Morris plunges a bowie knife into his heart. The Count crumbles into dust.
How many Bennet sisters are there, and what are they called?
There are five: Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Kitty and Lydia. Jane is the eldest, and Lydia is the youngest.
When does Catherine Earnshaw die?
She dies two hours after giving birth to her daughter, Cathy, on the night of her last stormy meeting with Heathcliff.
Who killed Charles McCarthy in The Boscombe Valley Mystery?
John Turner, a dying landowner whom McCarthy had blackmailed for years. Holmes keeps Turner's signed confession private unless it is needed to save McCarthy's son.
How many parent scales are there in the thaat and melakarta systems?
Hindustani music commonly uses ten thaats. The Carnatic melakarta system has 72 parent scales.
What did Aswatthaman do on the night after the battle?
He crept into the sleeping Pandava camp and killed Dhrishtadyumna, the sons of Draupadi and many others.
How did Sita prove her purity after Ravan's defeat?
She asked Lakshman to build a pyre and walked into the flames. The Lord of Fire himself lifted her out unharmed and declared her pure.
How does the jackal Curd-Face find out that a lion is hiding in his cave?
He calls out to the cave as if it always answers him. The lion, fooled, roars a greeting back, and the jackal runs off, since a cave that talks must hide an enemy.
What is the name of the Bolkonski family estate?
The estate is called Bald Hills. Old Prince Bolkonski lives there with his daughter Mary and keeps a very strict daily routine.
Who is Fedallah in Moby-Dick?
He is a mysterious Parsee whom Ahab secretly brought aboard with his own boat crew. He makes strange prophecies about how Ahab will die.
What happens when the creature saves a girl from drowning?
A man who was with her snatches the girl away and shoots the creature. His kindness is rewarded with a painful wound.
What crime is the Knave of Hearts accused of?
He is accused of stealing the tarts that the Queen of Hearts made on a summer day.
What is meend in Indian classical music?
Meend is a glide from one note to another. Along with andolan, gamak and kan-swar, it is one of the ornaments that many ragas depend on.
Who jilted Miss Havisham?
Compeyson, a smooth swindler, took money from her and never came on the wedding day. He was also Magwitch's old partner in crime.
What makes Jane go back to look for Rochester?
One night she seems to hear his voice calling "Jane! Jane! Jane!" from far away. The next day she leaves Moor House to find him.
Which member of the group dies in the last fight against Dracula?
Quincey Morris is fatally wounded. He dies happy, seeing that the red scar has gone from Mina's forehead.
Which house does Mr. Bingley take near the Bennets?
He rents Netherfield Park. His arrival delights Mrs. Bennet, who hopes he will marry one of her daughters.
How does Nelly find Heathcliff after his death?
He is lying in the old panelled bed with the window open and rain coming in. He had barely eaten in his last days.
Who really took the stones from the beryl coronet?
Sir George Burnwell, helped by Mary, the banker's niece. Arthur Holder was blamed, but he had actually been trying to get the coronet back.
Whom did Gandhari curse after the war?
She cursed Krishna, saying his own kinsmen, the Vrishnis, would destroy one another, just as the Kurus had done.
Why was Dasaratha cursed when he was young?
Hunting at night, he shot at a sound he took for an elephant drinking. It was a young hermit filling a pitcher, and the boy's father cursed Dasaratha to die grieving for a son.
What happens when the donkey insists on singing in the cucumber field?
The jackal warns him to keep quiet, but he brays anyway. The farmers wake, beat him, and tie a heavy mortar round his neck.
How did Krishna die?
He was lying in the forest, deep in thought, when a hunter named Jara mistook him for a deer. The arrow struck him in the heel.
In what order should a beginner practise a raga, according to the raga book?
Start with the tanpura and long Sa practice. Then sing slow aroha and avaroha, the pakad, short alap phrases, a bandish and simple taans, and listen to masters.
Who commands the Russian army at Borodino in Tolstoy's novel?
Kutuzov is the commander-in-chief. Tolstoy shows him as a patient old general who trusts time and the spirit of the troops more than clever plans.
How does Captain Ahab die at the end of the chase?
He darts his harpoon at Moby Dick, and the flying line catches him round the neck. It pulls him out of the boat and down into the sea.
How does Mary Shelley's novel end?
Victor dies on Walton's ship. The creature grieves over his body, then leaves on an ice raft and is soon lost in the darkness.
How does Alice's adventure in Wonderland end?
The whole pack of cards flies at her, and she wakes up on the bank with her head in her sister's lap. Her sister is brushing away leaves that have fluttered onto her face.
What does Pip tell Magwitch just before he dies?
He tells him that his lost daughter is alive, that she is a lady and very beautiful, and that Pip loves her. Magwitch dies in prison soon after.
How does Jane Eyre end for Jane and Rochester?
Jane marries Rochester, and they live at Ferndean. In time he recovers the sight of one eye and is able to see their first-born son.
Who is the 'bloofer lady' that the Hampstead children talk about?
She is Lucy, who has become a vampire after her death. She lures small children away at night.
Where does Darcy first propose to Elizabeth?
At the parsonage at Hunsford, where she is staying with Charlotte and Mr. Collins near Lady Catherine's estate, Rosings. Elizabeth angrily refuses him.
Who is Joseph at Wuthering Heights?
Joseph is the old servant there. He is sour and very religious, and he speaks in a thick Yorkshire dialect.
Why does Lord St. Simon's bride disappear after the wedding?
Hatty Doran sees her first husband, Frank, whom she believed dead, in the church. She leaves to rejoin him.
How did Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Kunti die?
They had gone to live in the forest as ascetics. A forest fire broke out, and they died in it.
How did Hanuman cross the sea to Lanka?
He climbed Mount Mahendra and leapt across the ocean in one mighty bound.
How does the rabbit Victory keep the elephants away from the Lake of the Moon?

He pretends to be a messenger of the Moon and says the Moon is angry with the elephants. When the elephant-king touches the water, Victory says he has angered the Moon even more, so the frightened king begs forgiveness and stays away.
Which notes can be komal, and which can be tivra?
Re, Ga, Dha and Ni can be komal, and only Ma can be tivra. Sa and Pa stay fixed.
Who fell first on the Pandavas' last journey to the mountains?
Draupadi fell first. Yudhishthira said it was because she had loved Arjuna more than her other husbands.
Who is Sonya in the Rostov household?
Sonya is a poor cousin brought up by the Rostovs. She loves Nikolai for years but finally writes to release him from his promise to her.
From which island do Ishmael and Queequeg sail?
They sail from Nantucket. They travel there from New Bedford together on a small packet boat.
On what kind of night does Victor bring the creature to life?
It is a dreary night in November, with rain pattering on the windows. When the creature opens its eyes, Victor is horrified and rushes out of the room.
Why, according to the Gryphon, are lessons called lessons?
He says it is because they lessen from day to day. The Mock Turtle adds that they had ten hours on the first day, nine the next, and so on.
Whom does Estella marry?
She marries Bentley Drummle, a rich, sulky young man. The marriage is very unhappy, and Drummle later dies after an accident with a horse he ill-treated.
Who is Mrs. Fairfax?
Mrs. Fairfax is the housekeeper at Thornfield. Jane at first thinks she owns the house, but she is only a distant relation of Mr. Rochester's family.
Why do the hunters put pieces of sacred wafer into Dracula's boxes?
The Count must rest in the earth he brought from his homeland. Sealing the wafer into each box makes that earth useless to him as a resting place.
What does Mr. Bennet tell Elizabeth when she refuses Mr. Collins?
He says her mother will never see her again if she does not marry Mr. Collins, and he will never see her again if she does.
Why does Hindley treat Heathcliff so badly?
As boys, Hindley was jealous because his father favoured Heathcliff. When his father dies, Hindley sends Heathcliff to work like a farm labourer.
Where do Holmes and Watson live together?
They share rooms at 221B Baker Street in London. After Watson marries, he moves out but still visits Holmes there.
Who was Ahalya, and how did Rama help her?
Ahalya was the wife of the sage Gautam, who cursed her to live unseen in penance. When Rama came to the hermitage, the curse ended and she was freed.
What happens to the girl who is married to a snake in the Panchatantra?
She serves her snake husband faithfully. One night he steps out of his snake skin as a handsome young man, and his father burns the skin so that he can never go back into it.
Why does Raga Marwa sound so restless?
Marwa leaves out Pa and leans on komal Re and tivra Ma, which creates tension. Its mood is linked to sunset.
Who fought Arjuna when he followed the sacrificial horse to Manipura?
His own son, Vabhruvahana. Arjuna fell in the fight, and Ulupi restored him to life with a special gem.
